hazards.evidence: Right-side stair handrail is short (spans only a few lower/mid steps) and does not run the full length of the staircase; left rail also appears to terminate before the bottom step, so a walker user lacks continuous graspable support.
Black cord/wire runs from the living-room/lamp area across the base of the staircase and the walking path, draping onto the lower step — directly in the route a walker would take.

Busy patterned carpet runner with no contrasting nosing makes step edges hard to distinguish, and several tread edges/sides show frayed or lifted carpet (light patches), creating a catch point for a walker or foot.
Stair treads are in shadow despite the single landing sconce; the lower and mid flight is dim, which combined with the patterned carpet obscures step definition.
Soft upholstered sofa with a throw in the living area beside the stairs; seating appears low/soft for safe sit-to-stand after hip/knee replacement.
